item.title: BMG Buys Publishing Catalog of The Living End’s Chris Cheney
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to this week's music update. We've got some exciting news from Australia, where BMG has just acquired the publishing catalog of Chris Cheney, the frontman and songwriter of the iconic rock trio, The Living End.
[Soft music transition]
Host: "This deal comes just days after The Living End was inducted into the 2026 ARIA Hall of Fame, a well-deserved recognition of their contributions to Australian music. With a career spanning decades, The Living End has built a reputation as a must-see live act, blending rockabilly, pop-punk, and indie grit to create a unique sound.
[Clip of "Second Solution / Prisoner of Society" plays in the background]
Host: "Their self-titled debut album, released in 1998, remains one of Australia's best-selling rock albums, featuring anthems like 'Second Solution / Prisoner of Society'. Over the years, the band has racked up an impressive list of accolades, including two number one albums, six ARIA Awards, and a slew of top 10 hits.
[Music transition]
Host: "Chris Cheney himself had some words to share about the deal, saying 'one of the great joys of being a musician is songwriting... songs can take weeks to write, or they can appear in minutes seemingly out of nowhere, they are the most wonderful, mysterious, powerful things!' He also expressed his gratitude to BMG, saying he's 'thankful and very honored' to have done the deal with a company that shares his passion for music.
[Clip of Heath Johns' quote plays]
Host: "Heath Johns, president of BMG Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia, commented, 'The Living End has been the soundtrack to countless Australian stories and memories... we are incredibly honored that Chris has chosen BMG as his forever home for these iconic publishing rights, and we look forward to finding new opportunities for them at home and abroad.'
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for today's update. Congratulations to The Living End on their well-deserved Hall of Fame induction, and we can't wait to see what the future holds for this iconic band. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you next time!"
